title: Route-level A/B testing — weekly notes (2026 W05)
content:
Week: 2026-W05 (Jan 26–Feb 1)

Owner: Dylan (Console & Tooling)
Note-taker(s): Dylan, Chloe
Standing sync: Tue/Thu 11:00 PT

---

1) TL;DR / status
- We’re unblocked enough to start wiring end-to-end “create experiment -> assignment -> exposure event emitted” in staging.
- Assignment library PR is in review; policy engine config model PR is close.
- Still open: deterministic hash inputs (what’s always present + privacy-safe) and policy precedence vs canaries/fallbacks.
- Telemetry schema is ~80% aligned but we need a hard call on which dimensions we allow in v1 to avoid cardinality surprises.

---

2) What shipped / progress this week
Backend / routing / assignment
- PR up for core assignment lib (bucketing + stickiness + retry behavior). Includes tests for stable assignment across retries (but we need to validate behavior for streaming reconnects separately).
  - Owner: Jordan / Jada
  - Link: GitHub:redwood/pr_18342_ab-testing-assignment-core
- Policy engine data model extended to include “experiment definition” and an early pass at precedence rules.
  - Owner: Ravi / Jordan
  - Link: GitHub:redwood/pr_18357_policy-engine-support-experiment-config

Console
- Chloe started API shape proposal for CRUD endpoints (create/update/validate/start/stop/rollback). Not in PR yet; doc exists in notes section + will go into ENG-2843.
- Kenji/Tessa provided first-pass copy for the “Validate config” step + warnings for overlapping rollouts.

Telemetry / analytics
- Logan + Nadia aligned on baseline metrics we must have (latency TTFT + E2E, token counts, cost attribution hooks, error/timeout).
- Draft exposure event schema is consistent with earlier rollout exposure logging patterns, but we need to decide if we log request_id or only a derived stable id.

SRE / operations
- Sean requested we treat “kill switch / emergency disable” as a first-class path, not an afterthought. Proposed: global experiment-disable flag + per-experiment disable action.

---

3) Current focus / in-flight work
- ENG-2841: integrate assignment into policy evaluation path (routing layer).
  - Open question: where do we compute assignment (gateway vs control plane vs router service)? We currently assume policy engine returns assignment deterministically based on request tags.
- ENG-2842: exposure event schema + ingestion contract.
  - Need final decision on allowed tags (experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, project_id???)
- ENG-2843: Console backend CRUD APIs.
  - Drafting validation rules (see section 6).

---

4) Blockers / risks
A) Deterministic assignment inputs (biggest blocker)
- We need a deterministic “hash key” that is (a) present across hosted + dedicated; (b) stable across retries; (c) privacy-safe; (d) hard to spoof.
- Candidate fields (from thread): tenant_id/project_id + api_key_id + optional customer-provided header (e.g., x-redwood-sticky-id).
- Risk: If we default to user_id-like headers, we’ll get missing values and variant flipping (bad UX) + support burden.
- Ask: platform decision this coming week.
  - Thread: Slack:eng-platform/1706812331

B) Policy precedence vs canary / fallback routing
- We need explicit precedence ordering. Otherwise “experiment” vs “canary rollout” interactions will be surprising.
- Proposal (tentative):
  1) Hard safety fallbacks (capacity / health / explicit blocklist)
  2) Route-level experiment assignment
  3) Canary rollout policies / gradual model rollouts
  4) Default route config
- Concern: Some teams expect canary rollout to always override experiments.
- Need ADR-level decision before we expose in Console.
  - Thread: Slack:eng-platform/1706904410

C) Metric cardinality / cost
- If we attach too many dimensions (project_id, route, model, variant, region, etc.) we risk a blowup.
- Need strict allowlist and documented “do not tag” list.
- Nadia asked for experiment_id+variant_id to be present in cost attribution, but we should not add route-level raw strings if we can avoid.

D) Streaming / retries semantics
- What happens when a request reconnects mid-stream?
- We need to ensure it doesn’t re-roll assignment and create duplicate exposure events.
- Proposed: compute a stable “exposure_id” per request attempt; dedupe downstream.

---

5) Decisions pending (need owners + dates)
1. Hash key / stickiness semantics (Owner: Jada + Jordan + Mina; due: Tue W06)
   - Decide default key + whether we require/encourage x-redwood-sticky-id.
   - Also decide stickiness duration and whether it’s per-request or per-session concept.

2. Precedence ordering (Owner: Ravi + Paula; due: Thu W06)
   - Finalize ordering + document “what wins” matrix for overlapping configurations.

3. Exposure event: include request_id? (Owner: Logan + Marcus; due: Thu W06)
   - Security stance: avoid request_id if it can be joined to PII.
   - Alternative: exposure_id derived from request metadata with one-way hashing.

4. Console terminology: “Control / Variant” naming (Owner: Tessa; due: Tue W06)
   - Support feedback already suggests confusion when customers name variants “A/B” but Console also labels “control”.

---

6) Notes / working decisions (not final)
Validation rules draft (Console + backend)
- Prevent experiments on routes with an active rollback in progress.
- Detect overlapping experiments on the same route + project. (We can allow overlap only if eligibility rules are disjoint; likely v1 = forbid.)
- Enforce traffic split sums to 100% and each variant >= 1% when running.
- Guardrail prerequisites: if experiment is >X% traffic, require guardrails enabled (latency/error thresholds) OR explicit “I acknowledge” (PM call).
- Ensure variants are compatible model family (tokenizer mismatch / context length differences) OR require “compat mode” warning.

Telemetry dimensions draft (v1)
- Required: experiment_id, variant_id, region, env, timestamp, route_fingerprint (not raw path), outcome(success/error), latency_ms, ttft_ms (if streaming), prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens.
- Optional: model_id (but watch cardinality), customer_tier (hosted/dedicated), http_status.
- NOT in v1: raw route path, user-provided headers, arbitrary customer labels.

---

7) Links (current week)
Linear
- ENG-2841 — ab assignment policy engine integration
- ENG-2842 — exposure event schema and ingestion
- ENG-2843 — console A/B testing CRUD APIs
- ENG-2844 — console results aggregation jobs (not started)
- ENG-2845 — dashboards and alerting (stub)
- ENG-2847 — security review (prep questions in progress)

GitHub
- GitHub:redwood/pr_18342_ab-testing-assignment-core
- GitHub:redwood/pr_18357_policy-engine-support-experiment-config

Slack
- Slack:eng-platform/1706812331 (hash inputs / request fields)
- Slack:eng-platform/1706904410 (precedence canary vs experiment)

---

8) Next week plan (2026 W06)
Engineering
- Land assignment lib PR + start integration into routing path behind feature flag.
- Write minimal “assignment contract test” in staging (send 1000 requests -> verify split approx matches) + verify sticky behavior across retries.
- Finalize exposure event schema (v1) with allowlisted tags; start ingestion validation tests.

Console
- Draft CRUD endpoint spec into ENG-2843 and start implementing create + validate endpoints.
- Add UI warnings for overlapping rollouts (even if we hard-block, we should explain why).

SRE / ops
- Sean to propose initial guardrail defaults (max latency regression, error rate). We’ll review for feasibility.
- Create a draft runbook outline (emergency disable / rollback) even before automation.

---

9) Asks / help needed
- Platform: confirm which request fields are available at assignment evaluation point (gateway/router) across Hosted + Dedicated.
- Security: quick sanity check on exposure event fields to avoid PII / joinability.
- Design: decision on variant naming + copy for “Validate” and “Stop/rollback” actions.

---

10) Open questions (parking lot)
- Do we support >2 variants in v1 UI or only A/B? (Backend likely supports N; UI complexity.)
- How do we represent “paused” vs “stopped” vs “rolled back”? (state machine needs to be clear.)
- For Dedicated: do we need capacity-aware guardrails (avoid shifting traffic onto a saturated pool) as a precondition?
